# Market report: 2026-11-02

## Market snapshot
1. **Stocks bounce, then fade as oil falls.** Stocks rebounded after Friday's selloff as oil slid on Mideast/US-Iran hopes, and futures showed oil below $100. By afternoon, CNBC reported the Nasdaq and S&P 500 turning negative on a continued rotation out of tech. 4. **Fewer Fed rate votes.** Chair Kevin Warsh said that in 2027 one meeting will focus only on strategy, with no rate vote or policy statement. [CNBC](https://news.google.?oc=5)

## Advisor angle
Clients holding borrowing or cash decisions face rate uncertainty: the Fed is paused, yet officials hint at hikes, and there will be fewer scheduled votes. An advisor would likely stress flexible plans (debt payoff, cash needs, staggered decisions) over betting on one rate path. Barron's notes fewer meetings could mean more uncertainty for stocks. ## Term of the day: Dilution
When a company pays for an acquisition by issuing new shares, each existing share represents a smaller slice of the company. Investors reportedly worried about this with Marvell's deal, since it had only $3.93 billion in cash as of Aug. 1.

## Interview talking point
"Marvell's drop on a $115 billion deal showed me that the market judges how an acquisition is paid for, not just whether the technology fits."
